news.title: Betway and betPawa Engage With Malawi Gambling Regulator Over 15% Tax Increase
news.summary: Malawi's Gaming and Lotteries Authority (MAGLA) opened talks with major brands including betPawa after a new law (effective end of December 2025) raised withholding tax on gambling winnings from 10% to 15% and removed tax-free thresholds.

news.title: BetPawa deposits disrupted amid Cameroon mobile-money routing dispute
news.publisher: Reported via industry/news aggregation (exact original publisher not confirmed)
news.summary: On 25-26 January 2025, deposits on betPawa and other betting platforms in Cameroon were disrupted when the government attempted to force all betting payments through a single provider (INTOUCH Cameroon); the decision was reversed within 48 hours.

news.title: Who owns betPawa?
news.summary: Multiple Ghanaian outlets reported in July 2023 that the betPawa brand is owned by Mchezo Limited, a Rwanda-based company, as part of coverage explaining the brand's ownership structure following its shareholder-distribution scheme.

news.title: pawaPass, Mchezo to distribute $2 million shares to betPawa customers
news.publisher: The Citizen (Tanzania) / BusinessDay NG / Daily News (Tanzania)
news.summary: In 2022, betPawa's parent Mchezo partnered with pawaPass (which holds a Trust and Corporate Service Provider licence from the Rwandan central bank) to distribute $2 million in shares to roughly 200,000 loyal betPawa customers, framed as a customer-shareholder/Africanisation initiative.

news.title: Consumer complaints against betPawa (withheld winnings, altered bet settlement, unresponsive support)
news.summary: Aggregated consumer-complaint sites record recurring user complaints against betPawa properties (e.g. betpawa.com, betpawa.ng) alleging withheld winnings, unilateral bet-market changes after settlement, and slow/unhelpful customer support responses; these are unverified individual consumer disputes rather than regulatory findings.

contradictions: The site under investigation (betpawa.ug) is a Uganda-market betting platform licensed only by Uganda's NLGRB, yet the investigation context (input country: Spain) implies the site/brand is reachable by and of concern to a Spanish audience; no corresponding DGOJ authorisation for this brand or any related entity was found, indicating potential unlicensed accessibility in Spain.

Domain WHOIS data for betpawa.ug (via third-party WHOIS aggregation) names the registrant as 'Mchezo IP Limited' of Kigali, Rwanda, while the entity publicly identified by Uganda's own regulator as the licensed operator is 'Chop Gaming Limited' - a different legal name, consistent with a brand-holding-company vs. local-licensee split typical of white-label/franchise gambling groups, and a structure that can obscure a single accountable entity for enforcement purposes.

Press reports consistently name 'Mchezo Limited' (Rwanda) as the owner of the betPawa brand, but WHOIS registrant data names the closely-related but distinct 'Mchezo IP Limited' - the precise legal relationship between these two similarly-named entities (and whether they are the same entity under different disclosure) could not be confirmed in this session.

This session's WebFetch tool returned HTTP 403 for every URL attempted, including unrelated control pages (e.g. google.com, en.wikipedia.org), preventing direct verification of the target site's own footer/terms disclosures, the live DGOJ register, Uganda's LGRB/URSB registers, and Rwanda's RDB register; all findings therefore rely on WebSearch-aggregated third-party snippets rather than primary-source confirmation, and should be re-verified once direct fetch access is restored.
analystNotes: Investigation method: the WebFetch tool was non-functional throughout this session, returning HTTP 403 Forbidden for every URL attempted - including the target site, WHOIS lookup pages, the DGOJ register, Uganda's LGRB site, OpenCorporates, and even unrelated control URLs (google.com, en.wikipedia.org, an igamingtoday.com article) - indicating a session-level tool failure rather than site-specific blocking or anti-bot measures. As a substitute, all findings in this brief were assembled via WebSearch, which aggregates snippets from third-party sources: WHOIS resellers (ip2whois.com), business-registry mirror/aggregator sites (Estonia's ariregister.rik.ee reflected via search, OpenCorporates commentary), a regulator's own social-media account (Uganda NLGRB on X), and African/industry press. Because no primary source was fetched directly, several facts that would normally be 'verified' (basis) have been downgraded to 'disclosed' or 'inferred' to reflect that only secondary reporting of the primary source was available, not the primary source itself. Headline findings for the enforcement case file: (1) betpawa.ug is operated locally under Uganda's NLGRB licensing regime by Chop Gaming Limited (T/A betPawa); (2) the wider betPawa brand is reported to be owned by a Rwanda-based entity, Mchezo Limited/Mchezo IP Limited, with platform technology attributed to pawaTech OU of Estonia (verified Estonian registry code 12551662); (3) no evidence of any Spanish DGOJ authorisation for betPawa, Mchezo, Chop Gaming, or pawaTech was found in DGOJ-related search results, consistent with this being an unlicensed-in-Spain operation, though this could not be confirmed against the live DGOJ register directly; (4) recurring unverified consumer complaints about withheld winnings and bet-settlement disputes were found on complaint-aggregator sites. Recommended next steps for a follow-up pass: re-run with working direct fetch access to (a) capture betpawa.ug's own footer/terms/licensing-page disclosures verbatim, (b) query the DGOJ public operator register directly for 'betPawa'/'Mchezo'/'Chop Gaming'/'pawaTech', (c) query Uganda's URSB and Rwanda's RDB registries for exact registration numbers and registered addresses of Chop Gaming Limited and Mchezo Limited/Mchezo IP Limited respectively, and (d) obtain a live, tool-verified WHOIS record for betpawa.ug rather than a search-engine-summarized one.
